solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Historian originally expressing views in press and TV register

indicators.note: originally points to the start of each word, so only their opening letters are kept
in places the kept letters inside the word for the news outlets that follows

blocks.note: newspapers and television together are the media
the first letters of these two words
a register is a list of names

explanation.surface: A historian first airs opinions in the papers and on television.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the front; 'in' is the insertion signal, placing the initials inside the media rather than linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A medievalist is a scholar or historian who specialises in the Middle Ages.

clue.text: Doctor initially braving disorderly crowd

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the opening letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor
first letter of braving

explanation.surface: A doctor bravely faces an unruly crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a large crowd of people that is out of control and liable to violence.

clue.text: Woman keeping record in warehouse

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so the woman's name wraps around the record

blocks.note: Dot is a woman's name, short for Dorothy
EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A woman stores a record in a warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse or warehouse where goods are kept.

clue.text: English ambassador inspired by PM's descriptive word

indicators.note: something inspired is breathed in, so the ambassador ends up inside the prime minister's name

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
William Pitt, father and son, were both British prime ministers
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An English diplomat takes his lead from the Prime Minister's choice of word.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'has' linking wordplay to definition: E + PIT(HE)T.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase describing a characteristic quality of someone, such as 'the Great'.

clue.text: Worthy naval officer capturing British frigate ultimately

indicators.note: capturing means taking prisoner and holding, so the officer's rank surrounds the abbreviation
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: an admiral commands a fleet
B is the abbreviation for British
last letter of frigate

explanation.surface: A worthy admiral seizes a British warship in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Admirable describes someone deserving respect and approval, which is what worthy means too.

clue.text: US soldier set up card-game in ice house

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means raised from bottom to top, so the soldier's letters run upwards

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier
loo is an old gambling card game

explanation.surface: An American soldier organises a game of cards inside a house of ice.
explanation.walkthrough: Loo, besides being British slang for a toilet, is an old card game played for stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is the dome-shaped Inuit shelter built from blocks of packed snow and ice.

clue.text: Given time, girl produces a square tile

blocks.note: Tess is a girl's name
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A girl with time on her hands makes a square tile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Given time' reads as a single phrase meaning eventually, but the girl comes first and the period follows her.
explanation.definitionFit: A tessera is one of the small square pieces of stone or glass used to make a mosaic.

clue.text: Antelope finally displaying character in Thessaly

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: last letter of displaying
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and Thessaly is in Greece

explanation.surface: An antelope at last shows its true nature in a Greek region.
explanation.definitionFit: The gnu, or wildebeest, is a large African antelope.

clue.text: Courage shown by everyone digging into bridge support

indicators.note: digging into means burrowing inside, so one word goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: a gantry is a bridge-like frame supporting cranes or signals
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everyone shows courage by excavating under a bridge's foundations.
explanation.definitionFit: Gallantry is bravery, especially in battle, as in medals awarded for gallantry.

clue.text: Where tubers are insufficiently crushed?

blocks.note: surface reading: potatoes and other tubers grow beneath the soil
setter's reading: not ground enough

explanation.walkthrough: Tubers grow below the surface, and the answer split in two means 'not ground enough', as with beans under-milled.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer means below the surface of the earth, where root vegetables like potatoes grow.

clue.text: Is balm apt somehow for such a church rite?

definitions.note: adjective: relating to the rite of christening

indicators.note: somehow says the letters come together in some unstated way, so they must be rearranged

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Asks whether a soothing ointment would suit a church ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: an anointing balm is indeed used at some christenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Baptismal means relating to baptism, the Christian rite of initiation with water.

clue.text: Compact offered for retail around India

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the past tense of retail wraps the letter for India

blocks.note: goods offered for retail have been sold
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A compact disc or make-up case put on sale in India.
explanation.definitionFit: Compact and solid both mean dense and firmly packed together.

clue.text: Baseball player in jug

blocks.note: first meaning: the player who throws the ball to the batter
second meaning: a large jug for pouring liquids

explanation.surface: A baseball player is locked up in jail, jug being slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: One word names both the baseball thrower and a large container with a handle and lip for pouring.

clue.text: A despicable person in professional theatre, not a fighting man

indicators.note: in places the words before it inside the short word for professional
not a tells us to leave out one letter A from the word for theatre

blocks.note: a pro is a professional
A plus rat, a despicable person
opera is musical theatre

explanation.surface: A scoundrel among the theatre professionals is no soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a' looks like part of the surface's denial, but it strips the A from OPERA.
explanation.definitionFit: A paratrooper is a soldier trained to be dropped into battle by parachute.

clue.text: Outdoor enclosure used in one's first broadcast

indicators.note: first means only the leading letter of the word before it is kept
used in places the enclosure inside the other pieces

blocks.note: first letter of one's
a pen is an enclosure for animals
to air a programme is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: An outdoor stockade appears in someone's debut programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Open-air means out of doors, not under any roof.

clue.text: Automated machine to hold up books?

blocks.note: to hold up a bank is to rob it
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a machine might be used to prop up a shelf of books.
explanation.definitionFit: A robot is a machine that carries out a series of actions automatically.

clue.text: Aussie missile's resonant sound echoed around back of house

indicators.note: around means encircling, so the two sound words surround the last letter
back of here picks the end of the following word to be enclosed

blocks.note: a boom is a deep resonant sound
the last letter of house
a sound that echoed rang out

explanation.surface: A missile's thunder reverberates around the rear of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: The two sound words together go around the end of house, so the enclosed letter lands between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A boomerang is the curved throwing weapon of Aboriginal Australians, so an Australian missile.

clue.text: Splash that's more effective outside health resort

indicators.note: outside means one word is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: more effective is better
a spa is a health resort

explanation.surface: Splashing about outdoors at a spa does you more good.
explanation.definitionFit: To bespatter is to splash or spatter with a liquid such as mud.

clue.text: Prissy son in Paris that friends finally ditch

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the closing letter of the next word is kept

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
que is French for that
amis is French for friends, carried on from in Paris
last letter of ditch

explanation.surface: A fussy son in Paris whose friends eventually drop him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' governs both the following words, so friends is in French too.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeamish means easily disgusted or shocked, which prissy similarly conveys of prim fastidiousness.

clue.text: To us, a sure assembly for the bottom drawer

definitions.note: a collection of things kept for marriage

indicators.note: an assembly is something put together from parts, so these letters are built into a new order

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone assures us that a piece of furniture is put together.
explanation.walkthrough: A bottom drawer is the British name for the linen and household goods a young woman gathered for married life, also called a hope chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride collects for her marriage, what was once kept in a bottom drawer.

clue.text: Braggart's display of force

blocks.note: a show is a display
taken as written
F is the symbol for force in physics

explanation.surface: A boaster puts on a show of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off is someone who boasts and tries to impress others, just like a braggart.

clue.text: Shy literary bear, do we hear, or beaver-like rodent?

indicators.note: do we hear asks the solver to judge the words by their sound, not spelling

blocks.note: coy means shy, and Pooh is A. A. Milne's bear

explanation.surface: Is the timid bear of children's books really a beaver-like creature?
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu, also called nutria, is a large South American water rodent that resembles a beaver.

clue.text: Thin, crisp biscuit — a marvellous thing!

blocks.note: first meaning: a dry savoury biscuit
second meaning: informal for something excellent

explanation.surface: Someone praises a crisp biscuit as wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a savoury wafer and, in British slang, something or someone excellent, as in 'it was a cracker of a goal'.

clue.text: Laborious exercises accepted by old woman

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the exercises go inside the old woman

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
PE is physical education, school exercises
Rose is a woman's name

explanation.surface: An elderly woman takes on a tiring workout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old woman' looks like a single unit, but it splits into O and a girl's name, with the exercises slotted between.
explanation.definitionFit: Operose is a rare formal word meaning involving much labour or industry.

clue.text: Good person, always seen around that compound

indicators.note: seen around means one word encloses the other

blocks.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever
ST is saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A good person is always present near that chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: An ester is an organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Gave a protégé expensive diamonds to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with means at the start, so the leading letters of the words are kept

blocks.note: taken as written
a ward is a young person under someone's protection
first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Someone gave a young favourite costly diamonds as a start.
explanation.definitionFit: Awarded means gave or granted something officially, such as a prize.

clue.text: The same girl climbing over the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means going upwards, so the letters that follow read from bottom to top

blocks.note: Di is a girl's name
OTT is the abbreviation for over the top

explanation.surface: The same girl goes too far in climbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to say the same thing again, as with ditto marks in a list.

clue.text: Gallery having trouble with image promotion?

blocks.note: PR is public relations, which promotes an image
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An art gallery is struggling with its publicity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' puts the trouble alongside the promotion, which comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prado in Madrid is one of the world's great art galleries.

clue.text: Con man's haystacks featured in Times with hesitation

indicators.note: featured in means appearing inside, so the haystacks sit within the letters for Times

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time, and two of them make Times
ricks are stacks of hay
er is the hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A swindler's haystacks feature in the newspaper with some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Times looks like the newspaper, but it is the plural of time abbreviated, giving two Ts.
explanation.definitionFit: A trickster is someone who deceives or cheats people, as a con man does.

clue.text: Twisted-sounding cereal plant

indicators.note: sounding means we go by how the word is said, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: wry can mean twisted or bent to one side

explanation.surface: Describes a cereal crop with a distorted sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Rye is a cereal grass grown for grain, used in bread and whisky.

clue.text: Fish brought back in this cheap paper

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the fish's name is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish is returned wrapped in cheap newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag is a dismissive word for a low-quality newspaper.

clue.text: Commotion involving amphibious troops in addition to that

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the commotion wraps around the troops

blocks.note: a furore is an outburst of public anger or excitement
the RM, the Royal Marines, Britain's sea-and-land soldiers

explanation.surface: A fuss involving the marines comes on top of everything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The troops are 'the RM', the Royal Marines with the definite article included, slotted into the commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Furthermore is an adverb meaning besides or moreover, adding a point to one already made.
